query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing molybdenum into the CoCrFeNi matrix to form a CoCrFeNiMo composite with integrated secondary phases (e.g., Ni/MoS₂–Ag–Cr₂O₃) will enable the in situ development of a stable, lubricious tribofilm across the full temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C. This tribofilm, enriched with MoS₂ and stable oxides, is expected to maintain a lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate relative to the base CoCrFeNi alloy.
generation.intervention: Compositional modification by adding a controlled amount of molybdenum to create a CoCrFeNiMo composite, processed via spark plasma sintering along with integrated secondary phases (Ni/MoS₂–Ag–Cr₂O₃)
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted in ambient air with temperatures ranging from room temperature to 800 °C and under a constant applied load
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, stable tribofilm composed of lubricious MoS₂ and accompanying oxides (such as Cr₂O₃) that adheres to the worn surface
generation.mechanism: The added molybdenum promotes tribochemical reactions that lead to the in situ formation of MoS₂ and stable oxide phases during sliding. These phases form a persistent lubricious layer that mitigates friction and wear across a wide temperature range by accommodating thermal expansion and oxidation processes.
generation.predicted_outcome: The CoCrFeNiMo composite is predicted to exhibit a lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate compared to the original CoCrFeNi alloy throughout the temperature range tested (25 °C to 800 °C).
generation.baseline: Sliding performance (coefficient of friction and wear rate) of the base CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy under identical temperature, load, and environmental conditions
generation.boundary: Results applicable for sliding conditions in ambient air with temperatures from room temperature (approximately 25 °C) up to 800 °C, under a constant load as defined by the standard testing protocol
generation.uncertainty: The optimal molybdenum concentration and the synergistic contributions of the integrated secondary phases require further investigation, and it is uncertain if the tribofilm will form efficiently at all tested temperatures without additional process tuning.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: a control group of the original CoCrFeNi alloy and an experimental group of the CoCrFeNiMo composite with integrated secondary phases, both fabricated via spark plasma sintering. Conduct sliding wear tests across a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C under identical constant load conditions in ambient air. Compare the friction coefficients and wear rates of both sets.
measurements: Coefficient of friction during sliding tests
Quantitative wear rate (e.g., volume loss or mass loss)
Surface and tribofilm characterization using SEM/TEM and XPS after testing
Phase and composition identification using XRD
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the CoCrFeNiMo composite does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in friction/coefficient and wear rate compared to the base CoCrFeNi alloy across the full temperature range, or if a continuous, lubricious tribofilm is not observed in microstructural analyses, the hypothesis will be falsified.
